name: hostname
description: Shows or sets the system's hostname.

flags.description: IP addresses the hostname resolves to / all local IPs.
Set hostname temporarily (use hostnamectl for persistence).

examples.explanation: The FQDN, resolved via /etc/hosts or DNS.
Changes the name immediately but reverts at reboot — for permanent changes use hostnamectl set-hostname.

about: The kernel stores the hostname (visible in /proc/sys/kernel/hostname); userland tools read and set it. Persistent hostnames on systemd systems belong to /etc/hostname, managed cleanly by hostnamectl. Name resolution of the hostname happens through /etc/hosts or DNS.
useCases: Quickly confirm which server you are on.
Check FQDN configuration on new servers.
mistakes: Setting the hostname with bare hostname and losing it at reboot.
Expecting hostname -i to work without /etc/hosts entries — it often fails or returns 127.0.0.2.
